newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: OPINION - Ivan Wong comments on Malaysian palm oil.
newsitem.headline: OPINION - Ivan Wong comments on Malaysian palm oil.

text.p: KUALA LUMPUR, March 21 - CPO production fell 75,900 tonnes or 13.1 percent to 503,400 tonnes in February. As expected, production in Peninsular Malaysia declined a modest 8.2 percent or 33,800 tonnes to 378,200 tonnes. East Malaysia suffered a bigger drop of 25.2 percent because of advise weather conditions. Compared to February last year when the country also celebrated Chinese New Year and Hari Raya within the same week, production registered a growth of 23.7 percent.

For the first-two months this year, production amounted to 1.083 million tonnes or 8.9 percent more than the same period last year. The month-on-month decline of 13.1 percent in February this year as compared to 24.4 percent a year earlier reflected the ability of most oil plam estates and land development schemes, especially those in Peninsular Malaysia, to clear their backlog of harvesting operations towards the end of the month. Consequently, we have scaled down the size of the March crop to adjust for the lack of harvest backlog brought forward.

On the basis of partail data available for first-half March, production for the whole month is estimated at 630,000 tonnes. This is around 125,000 tonnes or 25 percent more than February but two percent lower than the same month last year. We can expect production in the first-three months of this year to register an annual growth of 4.5 percent. Stocks of palm oil at end-February turned out to be much higher than our estimate. PORLA reported stocks rose 26,500 tonnes to 723,000 tonnes from 696,500 tonnes a month earlier and compared to our estimate of 675,000 tonnes.

The much larger than expected stocks reflected entirely poorer than estimated offtake, especially domestic disappearance. PORLA reported exports of palm oil fell sharply by nearly 32 percent to around 377,000 tonnes from 553,300 tonnes in January. We are of the opinion February exports were under estimated by some 50,000 tonnes, However, even assuming a February export figure of 425,000 tonnes, it still fell short of the year ago figure of 435,400 tonnes. Exports in March are estimated at around 545,000 tonnes, much better than February but also lower than the year ago figure of 567,900 tonnes.

With production registering positive growth but exports trailing year ago levels, the outcome can only be higher stocks. We thus estimate end-March stocks of palm oil to reach 710,000 tonnes as against 688,000 tonnes a year earlier and 723,000 tonnes in the preceding month. Palm oil price held steady in recent days and were more than 60 ringgit higher than the corresponding period of last year. suffice to say, we see limited upside potential from current levels unless we see a strong growth in export demand from April onward.
US stocks of SBO meanwhile rose to 2,203 million lbs at end February from 2,172 million lbs a month earlier and 1,532 million LBS a year ago. South American SBO for June/July was quoted at $515 FOB.
(The opinions expressed in this article represent the views of the author only. They should not be seen as necessarily reflecting the views of Reuters).
